prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT (Target Off Block Time) issued only if capacity/ground path allow, frozen at horizon unless recorded exception. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; forecasts from Flight Intent Message and performance history; arrival regulation when demand exceeds Airport Acceptance Rate, AAR); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; AAR per runway config; recalculates on config/weather/staffing/sector workload change); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT, Calculated Takeoff Time; Ground Delay Program; produces Pushback Window Token when window frozen); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; TOBT protecting CTT; CTT to TSM; revised metering advisories over queue threshold); North/South Runway Meter; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display; TOBT/remarks read-only unless coordination role); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf); Gate Conflict Detector (stand conflicts; Gate Reopening Memo); Time Synchronization Service; Arrival Regulation Console (Nightjar); Integrated Tactical Management Position; Sector Load Monitor; Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; routes Tactical Regulation Proposal for acknowledgement); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; Fuel Truck Hold Advice; MUST refresh apron layer within 5 s of validated surface event); Collaborative Decision Log and Audit Event Ledger (all actions, recommendations, acknowledgements, rejected alternatives); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Handling Resource Planner; Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard); Business Rules Registry (thresholds for alerting/approval/publication per state); Identity Access Service; Digital Briefing Room. Accepted measures yield CTT updates, Slot Compliance State changes or capacity annotations. Diversion triggers: fuel-threshold holding, approach loss, sector saturation, runway below minimum rate. Modes (declared by Airport Duty Manager after coordination): Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State; also Winter Operating Mode. Objective: prevent airborne holding. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin); Slot Coordinator (Halcyon); Airline Operations Coordinator (AOC, Saffron); Aircraft Operator Representative; Tower Supervisor; Airspace Sector Planner (Sector Load Monitor); Military Airspace Liaison; Meteorology Briefing Officer (verifies weather); Ground Handling Dispatcher.

New part:
S443: Surface constraints are treated as tactical capacity inputs because they can change the feasible order, timing, and routing of aircraft after demand has already been balanced against airspace capacity.
S444: The Regional Flow Platform correlates surface equipment conditions with flight intent, stand assignment, and runway plan data before recommending any change to the active tactical plan.
S445: The Surface Surveillance Adapter provides current movement area occupancy and equipment status indicators to the Ramp Movement Board and the Tower Sequence Manager.
S446: When a gate bridge, ground power unit, fuel hydrant point, or marked taxilane is unavailable, the Ramp Control Lead verifies whether the condition blocks a single movement, a stand group, or a wider apron route.
S447: The Airport Duty Manager records the operational significance of the condition in the Airport CDM Portal so that all planning components use the same constraint description.
S448: The Capacity Assessment Module converts persistent surface constraints into reduced stand throughput, extended turn buffers, or modified taxi-out assumptions.
S449: Fuel vehicle holds affect the tactical plan by delaying off-block readiness even when crew, passengers, and aircraft serviceability are otherwise complete.
S450: Tower Sequence Manager uses the hold advice to prevent a departure from being sequenced ahead of a fueling constraint that is still active.
S451: The Airline Operations Coordinator remains responsible for confirming whether the affected flight should keep its Target Off Block Time, request a new value, or accept a later Calculated Takeoff Time.
S452: Airline Interface Adapter produces the Late Baggage Tag List when baggage reconciliation data indicates that departure readiness may be overstated.
S453: Runway metering advisories are applied when the departure queue, runway crossing demand, or runway occupancy trend indicates that uncontrolled pushback would create an unstable surface queue.
S454: North Runway Meter reduces the departure release rate when surface surveillance shows that runway-entry queues are approaching the metering threshold.
S455: The South Runway Meter applies the same planning principle to its assigned runway stream while preserving separation from arrival regulation actions.
S456: The Departure Metering Service translates runway metering limits into candidate pushback spacing for the Slot Allocation Engine.
S457: If the metering action affects a regulated flight, the Slot Coordinator reviews the relationship between the Calculated Takeoff Time and the proposed surface release time before accepting the change.
S458: Apron congestion advisories are generated when the Ramp Movement Board shows conflicting pushbacks, blocked lead-in lines, saturated holding points, or insufficient room for safe wingtip clearance.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
